name: ChemElucid
description: ChemElucid is an interactive evaluation environment for AI agents on molecular structure elucidation from NMR spectroscopy. The release pairs (a) 18 process-graded core molecules with expert reasoning DAGs across CNMR, HNMR, and combined modes, and (b) 48 withheld-probe molecules sampled from nmrshiftdb with hidden canonical SMILES used for outcome-only transfer evaluation. The artifact ships a public agent surface, a hidden grader, and a CLI for running and grading episodes.
citeAs: @misc{chemelucid_2026, title={ChemElucid: Diagnosing Scientific Agents in Molecular Structure Elucidation}, author={Anonymous Authors}, year={2026}, note={NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets track submission.}}
rai:dataCollection: Core molecules (18) are curated from open-access chemistry references and published NMR catalogs; their identities are public because process annotations require expert authoring. Withheld-probe molecules (48) are sampled with seed=42 from a 150-row nmrshiftdb-derived candidate pool, stratified to match the core distribution along heavy-atom count, degree of unsaturation, and ring count. Source database license: nmrshiftdb is CC-BY-SA 3.0; only canonical SMILES, peak lists, formula, solvent, and frequency are redistributed. The original nmrshiftdb identifier is anonymized in agent-facing files (probe_001..probe_048).
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of LLM agents on interactive scientific reasoning, with focus on whether final-answer accuracy reflects evidence-grounded investigation or benchmark-specific shortcutting. Process metrics (information acquisition, expert-DAG checkpoint coverage, dependency topology) make trajectory behavior auditable.
rai:dataLimitations: The 18 core molecules skew toward small drug-like aromatic structures. The 48 withheld-probe molecules draw from natural-product-leaning entries with higher heavy-atom count and ring count than the core. Stereochemistry annotation is shallow. Spectra are publication-derived and may carry solvent- and instrument-specific shift biases that are not modeled. The release evaluates a single time point and is not a longitudinal contamination certificate.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset contains no personal data, no human-subjects data, and no sensitive content. All molecules are small organic compounds documented in open-access chemistry sources.
rai:dataBiases: Selection bias: core molecules favor drug-like aromatic chemistry; probe molecules favor natural-product space, reflecting the source pool composition. Both sets exclude organometallics, large biopolymers, and most stereochemistry-rich systems.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: ChemElucid makes agentic scientific reasoning more auditable by separating final-answer accuracy from evidence acquisition and tool-use process metrics. Potential negative impact: benchmark overfitting, leakage of hidden answers, or use of the environment as a proxy for real laboratory structure elucidation without expert review. Mitigations include a public/private data split, a leakage audit, hidden grader-side SMILES for probe tasks, explicit budgeted tools, and documentation that the benchmark is intended for evaluation research rather than safety-critical chemical or clinical decision-making.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Core-18 expert DAG curation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Authors curated 18 molecule tasks with 13C, 1H, and combined NMR surfaces plus hidden expert reasoning DAG checkpoints for process grading. RDKit-based motif checks were used to validate structural ground truth where applicable.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Withheld-probe sampling
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Authors sampled 48 probe molecules from a 150-row nmrshiftdb-derived pool using seed=42, with quotas along heavy-atom count, degree of unsaturation, and ring count; the probes are outcome-only graded.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Public/private data split
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Agent-facing files contain formula and spectra only. Canonical SMILES, source identifiers, legacy aliases, and expert DAGs are stored in private grader files and are not served to evaluated agents.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Preprocessing and validation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Preprocessing normalizes identifiers, parses spectra, computes descriptors, builds deterministic manifests, and runs leakage checks to ensure agent-facing files exclude hidden answers.

distribution.name: probe_48_manifest.csv
distribution.description: Hidden ground-truth manifest for the 48-molecule withheld-probe layer. Used by the grader; not exposed to evaluation agents.

distribution.name: probe_spectra_cnmr
distribution.description: 48 agent-facing 13C NMR spectrum files. One JSON per probe molecule; contains formula, peaks, solvent, and frequency only. SMILES, InChI, and source identifiers are excluded by construction.

distribution.name: core_18_public_tasks
distribution.description: Agent-facing task files for the 18 process-graded core molecules. One file per molecule per spectrum mode (CNMR, HNMR, COMBO). Hidden answers (SMILES) are stored separately under data_split/private_grader_data/ and are not exposed in these files.

distribution.name: core_18_private_grader
distribution.description: Hidden grader files (canonical SMILES + reasoning DAG checkpoints) for the 18 core molecules. Used only by the grader CLI; never returned to the agent loop.

distribution.name: nmrshiftdb_scale150.csv
distribution.description: 150-row nmrshiftdb-derived candidate pool from which the 48 probe molecules were sampled with seed=42. Provenance only; not used at evaluation time.

recordSet.name: withheld_probe_48
recordSet.description: The 48-molecule withheld-probe layer. Outcome-only graded (InChI exact match + Morgan/2/2048 Tanimoto). No expert-DAG annotation; no L2 or L3 process metrics.

field.name: smiles_hidden
field.description: Canonical SMILES of the hidden ground-truth structure. Visible to the grader, never returned to the agent.

field.name: source_id
field.description: nmrshiftdb source entry id, e.g., nmrshiftdb2:2500. Provenance only; not exposed in agent-facing spectrum files.

field.name: heavy_atoms
field.description: Heavy-atom count (HAC) of the ground-truth structure. Used for difficulty stratification.

field.name: num_peaks
field.description: Count of distinct 13C NMR peaks in the source spectrum.

field.name: has_hnmr
field.description: Boolean: whether a 1H NMR spectrum is also released for this probe.

field.name: sampling_seed
field.description: Random seed (=42) used to draw this probe from the nmrshiftdb pool.

field.name: legacy_internal_id
field.description: Internal alias used by the curation pipeline (canary_001..canary_048). Documented for reproducibility; the public-facing ID is probe_id. The agent-facing 13C NMR spectrum file is named data/withheld_probe/spectra/{probe_id}_CNMR.json.

recordSet.name: core_18_process_graded
recordSet.description: The 18 process-graded core molecules. Each molecule has agent-facing task files (CNMR, HNMR, COMBO) under data_split/public_task_data/ and a hidden grader file under data_split/private_grader_data/. Three trajectory metrics (L1, L2, L3) are computed per episode against the expert reasoning DAG.

field.name: molecule_id
field.description: Public molecule identifier (the directory name under data_split/public_task_data/), e.g., 2_4_dimethyl_aniline.

field.name: spectrum_type
field.description: One of CNMR, HNMR, COMBO. Indicates which spectral modality the agent receives.

field.name: molecular_formula
field.description: Molecular formula of the ground-truth structure, exposed to the agent.

field.name: spectrum_peaks
field.description: 13C peak list (CNMR or COMBO mode) or 1H peak list (HNMR mode) exposed to the agent.
